chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it to Dawood al-Raqqi or someone else, said:

While we were seated in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), a man passed by with a slaughtered swallow in his hand. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) leapt towards him until he took it from his hand, then he pressed it into the ground and said (peace be upon him): 'Has your scholar or your jurist ordered you with this? My father informed me from my grandfather that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the killing of six, among them was the swallow.'

And he said: 'Its circling in the sky is regret for what was done to the People of the Household of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and its glorification is the recitation of 'Al-Hamdu Lillahi Rabbil-'Alameen'. Do you not see it saying 'Wa la ad-dalleen' (and not those who go astray)?'

key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ: The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the Worlds (Al-Fatiha opening)

ai.seo_question: What are the six creatures forbidden to be killed according to Shia hadith, and what is the significance of the swallow?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the high status of the swallow by questioning the religious authorities (*fuqaha*) on its permissibility, citing the Prophet’s prohibition of killing six specific creatures. The narration uniquely links the bird’s natural behavior to cosmic grief, interpreting its flight as mourning for the Ahl al-Bayt and its chirping as the recitation of Surah Al-Fatiha, specifically highlighting the verse 'Wa la ad-dalleen' (and not those who have gone astray).
